newsitem.title: USA: CompUSA CEO says January sales look good.
newsitem.headline: CompUSA CEO says January sales look good.

text.p: CompUSA Inc Chief Executive Officer Jim Halpin said 1997 retail sales were "off to a good start" in January, fuelled by strong demand for Intel Corp's new multimedia MMX chip, but he cautioned that the strong comparison with January 1996 sales may be misleading.
"It appears consumers are already adopting the MMX processor and so far the response has exceeded our expectations," Halpin said on a conference call.
He said Microsoft Corp's new Office 97 software, which was also introduced in January, is selling "very well."

"When we look at our results so far we ought to be mindful of the fact that last January was impacted by a number of winter storms and that new product transitions took place in February last year versus January this year," Halpin said.

CompUSA earlier reported net income of $23.7 million, or $0.25 per share, in its second fiscal quarter ending Dec. 28, up from $18.7 million, or $0.20 per share, in the second quarter of fiscal year 1996.
The earnings were in line with industry analysts' lowered expectations.

Halpin said earnings were hurt by a softening of computer retail sales over the Christmas period but said CompUSA had outperformed its major competitors and expected to increase its market share as rivals begin closing stores.

Tandy Corp last month said it was selling all 17 of its Incredible Universe superstores and closing 19 of its Computer City stores. Halpin said other competitors were scaling back their offerings of computer products.

"We believe these changes could result in as much as $2 billion in orphaned or abandoned sales. CompUSA plans to take advantage of this unique opportunity to increase our share of the total PC market," Halpin said.
